title: How Much Is Homeowners Insurance in Florida? 2026 Costs by County
dek: The state average is about $3,750 a year, but on the coast it runs from about $190 a month on the Nature Coast to about $655 in the Keys. Here is every beach county, cheapest to priciest, and what moves your own quote.
body:
The average Florida homeowners policy with wind coverage costs about $3,750 a year, or roughly $313 a month, according to the state Office of Insurance Regulation's July 2026 report. On the coast the county averages range from about $2,300 a year in Wakulla County, south of Tallahassee, to about $7,900 a year in the Florida Keys.

The short version: the Southeast Florida coast and the Keys cost the most, the Northeast Florida coast and the Nature Coast cost the least, and most of the Gulf and Panhandle sits in between. Your own quote can land well above or below your county's average depending on the house.

For comparison, inland Sumter County, home of The Villages, averaged about $2,105 a year, one of the lowest in the state.

Why the same house costs twice as much in different counties

Wind risk is most of it. Monroe County's average is about $7,863 a year with wind coverage, but only about $1,871 without it, according to the same state report. Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach are all over $5,900 for the same reason: dense, valuable coastline that hurricanes have hit hard before.

The cheaper coastal counties share a pattern too. The Northeast Florida coast, from Fernandina Beach down through St. Augustine and Flagler Beach, has seen far fewer direct hurricane strikes over the last 170 years than the Panhandle or South Florida. Our guide to what to check before you buy in hurricane season covers what that means for a specific house. The Nature Coast towns like Crystal River have lower home values and fewer big claims, which keeps averages down.

Are Florida insurance rates going down?

Yes, slowly. Average premiums with wind coverage fell in 51 of Florida's 67 counties between the state's January and July 2026 reports. Citizens, the state backed insurer of last resort, got approval for an average 8.7% statewide rate cut for 2026, its first decrease since 2015. Citizens has also shrunk to about 293,000 policies in June 2026 from about 1.4 million in 2023, as private companies took policies back. Since 2024, 44 insurers have asked the state for rate decreases.

That does not mean your renewal will drop. A cut in the average can still mean an increase on an older house.

What changes your own quote

  • Roof age and type. This is the big one. Carriers look hard at older shingle roofs, and a roof near the end of its life can mean a much higher price or fewer offers. Ask the seller for the roof permit date.
  • Wind mitigation report. A short inspection that documents hurricane straps, roof deck nailing and impact windows. Credits from a good report can cut the wind part of a premium a lot. Ask the seller for theirs.
  • Four point inspection. Older homes usually need one covering roof, electrical, plumbing and the water heater before a carrier will write the policy.
  • Hurricane deductible. Usually 2% or 5% of the dwelling coverage, not a flat dollar amount. On a $400,000 policy, a 5% deductible is $20,000 out of pocket per hurricane season.
  • Distance to the water and elevation. A house a mile inland on the mainland usually prices better than the same house on a barrier island.

Flood insurance is a separate bill

None of the averages above include flood. Standard homeowners policies do not cover rising water, so flood is a separate policy, either through FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program or a private carrier. Lenders require it in high risk zones, and plenty of Florida flood claims come from outside those zones. Check how a town scores in our flood risk rankings and get a flood quote on the exact address before you make an offer.

Condos are different

If you buy a condo, the association insures the building and you buy a smaller policy for the inside of your unit, usually far cheaper than a house policy. The catch is that the building's insurance shows up in your monthly dues, and a big premium increase or storm deductible can become a special assessment. Ask for the association's insurance declarations page and budget before you buy.

How to get a real number before you buy

Get at least two quotes on the specific address while you are under contract, ideally one from an independent agent who can shop several carriers. Bring the roof age, the wind mitigation report and any four point inspection. If the quote comes back high, it is usually the roof, and that is something to negotiate on. Our longer guide, what nobody tells you about Florida home insurance, walks through the rest.

Sources: Florida Office of Insurance Regulation, Property Insurance Stability Report, July 1, 2026 (county averages as of March 31, 2026); Newsweek reporting on the same report (statewide average); Citizens Property Insurance policy counts (June 2026); Florida OIR Citizens 2026 rate order.
faq: How much is homeowners insurance in Florida per month?

The statewide average for a policy with wind coverage is about $3,750 a year, or roughly $313 a month, per the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation's July 2026 report. Coastal county averages run from about $190 a month in Wakulla County to about $655 in the Keys.
Which Florida beach county has the cheapest homeowners insurance?
Among the coastal counties we cover, Wakulla, Hernando, Citrus and Flagler have the lowest averages, all under about $2,500 a year. On the Atlantic, Flagler County averages about $2,488.
Which Florida county has the most expensive homeowners insurance?
Monroe County, the Florida Keys, at about $7,863 a year on average with wind coverage, followed by Palm Beach, Broward and Miami-Dade.
Does Florida homeowners insurance include flood?
No. Flood is a separate policy through FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program or a private carrier, and it is not included in these averages.
Are Florida home insurance rates going down in 2026?
On average, slowly. Premiums fell in 51 of 67 counties in the first half of 2026 and Citizens got an average 8.7% cut, but an older roof or house can still see an increase.
